data.title: rpx
data.tagline: A relative size unit converted according to a mini program page’s width
data.learningOutcome: Predict that 750rpx spans the page width, while a fixed px length keeps its pixel size.
data.description: When page width is 375px, 600rpx is 300px; at 450px it is 360px. Both occupy 80% of page width. Relative sizing does not automatically reflow columns or prevent long text from overflowing.

learning.assumes: You have compared a mini program on different screen widths.
learning.outcome: Predict that 750rpx spans the page width, while a fixed px length keeps its pixel size.

distinctions.label: px
distinctions.explanation: A fixed CSS pixel length does not convert with page width as rpx does. CSS pixels are not physical device pixels.

distinctions.label: Responsive layout
distinctions.explanation: Changes arrangement when space is insufficient. rpx scales dimensions but does not choose a new layout.

explanation.title: Page width is the reference
explanation.text: Displayed CSS pixels = rpx value × page width in CSS pixels ÷ 750. The reference is page width, not physical pixel density.

explanation.title: Keep content readable
explanation.text: Scaling margins and widths can help. Long labels and columns still need wrapping and layout decisions at actual device widths.

data.boundary: Replacing every px value with rpx does not guarantee a good layout. Text size, touch areas, and wider screens require checking separately.

lessonPractice.title: A page grows from 375px to 450px wide. A strip uses width: 750rpx. What happens?

options.label: It grows to 450px and still spans the page
options.feedback: 750rpx represents full page width, so its displayed width follows the page.

options.label: It remains 375px, leaving room beside it
options.feedback: That is the behavior of a fixed 375px length, not 750rpx.

options.label: It becomes 750 physical pixels on the display
options.feedback: rpx is based on page width; it is not a count of physical pixels.

data.agentPrompt: Set this mini program booking button to 600rpx, retaining centering and its label. At page widths of 375px and 450px it should occupy about 80%. Check long labels and landscape too; fix the layout if content overflows or grows too large instead of merely shrinking text.
